newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: FORECAST - Stork net seen up on Fokker deal.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Stork net seen up on Fokker deal.

text.p: Dutch engineering group Stork NV is expected to post a profit rise for 1996 of about 20 percent on March 4, largely reflecting effects of the Fokker Aviation unit it bought last year, analysts say.
Forecasts for the 1996 net profit ranged from 122 to 135 million guilders, with consensus at about 129 million. In 1995, Stork posted a net profit of 108.3 million guilders.

Steef Bergakker of IRIS/Rabo Securities, whose profit estimate of 133.2 million guilders was at the higher end of the range, said he expected Fokker Aviation to have contributed some 15 million guilders to Stork's 1996 profits.
Stork bought the profitable maintenance and components units when planemaker Fokker went bankrupt last year.
Bergakker said Stork had indicated that Fokker Aviation would contribute about 600 million guilders to its 1996 turnover and a modestly positive profit in this transition year.
"You could guess at what modestly means but I have made an estimate (of the profit contribution) of about 15 million guilders," Bergakker said.
In a recent research report, Wijnand Heineken of Bank Labouchere also said Fokker Aviation (FA) will have a positive impact on Stork's 1996 results and earnings per share.
"The FA acquisition gives a boost to (Stork's) EPS growth," the Labouchere report said.

IRIS/Rabo Securities' Bergakker said he expected results at Stork's industrial systems and components division to have steadied or even slightly fallen last year, but results at the industrial services unit were expected to have clearly improved.

But he added that Stork will probably give no separate figures for Fokker Aviation. It will probably book two-thirds of the FA results with the systems and components division and the other third with industrial services, making the performance of Stork's traditional activities somewhat opaque.
Both Labouchere and IRIS/Rabo Securities rate the Stork shares at a Buy at present levels.
"Although Stork is a cyclical, we consider the share undervalued," Labouchere said.
"Compared with the rest of the Dutch share market Stork is still worth buying," Bergakker of IRIS/Rabo Securities said.
